name: ocfs2_read_virt_blocks
prose: Precondition: inode is an ocfs2 inode, v_block is the first virtual (file) block, nr the number of blocks to read, bhs an array of nr buffer_head pointers (entries may be NULL, or may be buffers from an earlier readahead call whose b_blocknr matches), flags the OCFS2_BH_* flags, validate an optional validator (ocfs2/extent_map.c:974-1045, int ocfs2_read_virt_blocks(struct inode *inode, u64 v_block, int nr, struct buffer_head *bhs[], int flags, int (*validate)(struct super_block *sb, struct buffer_head *bh)); the packet item was an unnamed fragment and is the main loop of this function). Postcondition: returns 0 on success or a negative errno; the only return is 'return rc' at 1044. If the last requested block lies at or beyond i_size it BUG_ON(!(flags & OCFS2_BH_READAHEAD)) and returns 0 without reading (goto out at 990). Otherwise, while done < nr it takes ip_alloc_sem with down_read_trylock (failure: rc = -EAGAIN with an error message, loop ends), maps the next run with ocfs2_extent_map_get_blocks (nonzero rc: stop with that error; the semaphore is released first), treats an unmapped hole (p_block == 0) as -EIO, limits count to min(nr - done, p_count), asserts (BUG_ON) that any non-NULL bhs[done + i] already has b_blocknr == p_block + i, reads the run with ocfs2_read_blocks (error: stop with it) and advances done by count. So on failure bhs entries before done may have been read and the later ones are untouched; rc holds the first error.
note: item was 'unnamed-batched-read-loop (fragment)' dropped; the slice 1023-1047 is the tail of ocfs2_read_virt_blocks (extent_map.c:974-1045; slice cut head), so FIXED under the real name per rule 6.

name: ocfs2_rename
prose: Precondition: the VFS holds i_rwsem on the parent directories for the rename; old_dentry is positive, new_dentry is positive or negative; flags must be 0 (ocfs2/namei.c:1206-1707, static int). Postcondition: returns 0 or a negative errno; 'return -EINVAL' at 1237 if flags is non-zero (before anything is done), otherwise 'return status' at 1706 after the common cleanup label bail. Sequence: dquot_initialize on both directories; igrab of new_inode; for a directory moved between different parents it takes the cluster rename lock and fails with -EPERM if the new parent is a descendant of the old inode (status 1) or with the error of ocfs2_check_if_ancestor; ocfs2_double_lock on both parents; -EACCES if new_dir->i_nlink is 0; -EIO if no buffer for either directory; it locks old_inode (ocfs2_inode_lock_nested; its error, silently for -ENOENT) and deletes its remote dentry lock; for a directory moving to a new parent it finds '..' (-EIO on failure or if the parent block disagrees) and returns -EMLINK if new_dir has the maximum number of links and the target does not exist; the name lookup in old_dir must give old_inode's block (-ENOENT otherwise); it looks up the target name in new_dir (only -ENOENT is tolerated as 'does not exist'; -ENOENT if a target inode was expected but the entry is gone; -EACCES if a target appeared that the VFS did not see or its block disagrees); an existing target is locked (error), its remote dentry lock deleted, and, if it is a directory or has i_nlink == 1, an orphan directory entry is prepared (should_add_orphan); a non-existent target gets ocfs2_check_dir_for_entry and ocfs2_prepare_dir_for_insert. It starts a transaction (error: bail); an existing target directory must have i_nlink == 2 and be empty (-ENOTEMPTY otherwise); the target entry is updated to point at old_inode and the target's link count is reduced (set to 0 for a directory) with the target added to the orphan directory when needed, or for a new name ocfs2_add_entry is called. It updates old_inode's ctime, then finds and deletes the old directory entry (if either step fails it reports ocfs2_error 'new entry ... is added, but old entry ... is not deleted' unless the journal is aborted, and bails with the error), adjusts link counts and times, updates '..' for a moved directory (error: bail) and marks the directories dirty. If old_dir's link count changed it rewrites it in old_dir_bh, but if old_dir_bh is NULL it only logs an error and does not update the on-disk count (the function still returns 0). Finally ocfs2_dentry_move and status = 0. bail: commits the transaction, unlocks the orphan directory, new and old child inodes, parent directories and the rename lock, syncs the old inode's buffers when a target existed, drops new_inode and the lookup results and the buffer heads, and returns status.
note: slice cut head (function at 1206-1707, slice 1551-1805). reviewer round 15 right: ocfs2/namei.c:1641-1646 logs 'need to change nlink for old dir ... but bh is NULL' and skips the on-disk link count update, after which status = 0 at 1663 is returned.

name: ocfs2_mv_orphaned_inode_to_new
prose: Precondition: dir is the (unlocked) directory to link into, inode is an orphaned ocfs2 inode (OCFS2_ORPHANED_FL set, link count 0) of this filesystem, dentry names a not-yet-existing entry in dir; the caller holds references on dir and inode and holds no cluster lock on dir (it is taken here) (ocfs2/namei.c:2789-2928, int ocfs2_mv_orphaned_inode_to_new(struct inode *dir, struct inode *inode, struct dentry *dentry)). Postcondition: returns 0 on success or a negative errno at line 2927 (and an earlier direct 'return status' at 2812). On success the inode is removed from this slot's orphan directory, its ORPHANED flag and orphaned slot are cleared on disk, its link count is set to 1, it is added to dir under the new name with ocfs2_add_entry, the dentry lock is attached and d_instantiate(dentry, inode) is called. Errors: the error of ocfs2_inode_lock(dir, ..., 1) is returned at 2812 with nothing held; -ENOENT (to leave) if dir's i_links_count is 0; the error of ocfs2_check_dir_for_entry (name already exists) or ocfs2_prepare_dir_for_insert; -ENOENT if the orphan directory system inode cannot be obtained; if ocfs2_inode_lock(orphan_dir_inode) fails it unlocks the VFS inode lock and iputs the orphan directory inode and goes to leave (without ocfs2_inode_unlock on it); a failure of ocfs2_read_inode_block, ocfs2_start_trans (handle left NULL), ocfs2_journal_access_di, ocfs2_orphan_del, ocfs2_add_entry or ocfs2_dentry_attach_lock goes to orphan_unlock or out_commit respectively. In the add-entry and attach-lock failure cases the inode has already been removed from the orphan directory and its on-disk flags changed in the transaction, which is still committed (out_commit calls ocfs2_commit_trans), so on those errors the changes are not rolled back by this function. Cleanup: out_commit commits the transaction; orphan_unlock releases the orphan directory's cluster lock, VFS lock and iput; leave releases the cluster lock on dir, the buffer heads (di_bh, parent_di_bh, orphan_dir_bh) and the directory lookup result.
note: item was 'unnamed_orphan_reinsert_function'; the slice 2822-2949 is the tail of ocfs2_mv_orphaned_inode_to_new (namei.c:2789-2928; slice cut head), then the ocfs2_dir_iops table, so FIXED under the real name. reviewers right: round 1 (the early return at 2812 and the leave path before the orphan lock skip the orphan-directory cleanup); round 2 (a failure of ocfs2_inode_lock(orphan_dir_inode) still does inode_unlock and iput, 2847-2853).

name: ocfs2_update_last_group_and_inode
prose: Precondition: handle is a running journal handle, bm_inode is the global bitmap inode with dinode buffer bm_bh, group_bh is the buffer of the last group descriptor of that bitmap, first_new_cluster is the first new cluster and new_clusters (int) the number of clusters being added to that group; the added bit count new_clusters * cl_bpc must fit in a u16 (num_bits is u16, line 111) and bg_bits plus it must not overflow u16 (ocfs2/resize.c:77-176, static int). Postcondition: returns 0 or a negative errno through the single 'return ret' at 175. It takes journal write access on group_bh (error: out, nothing changed), then in the group descriptor adds num_bits = new_clusters * cl_bpc to bg_bits and bg_free_bits_count, and, if the backup-superblock feature is on, recomputes backup superblock positions (ocfs2_calc_new_backup_super) and subtracts the number of new backup blocks from bg_free_bits_count; it recomputes bg_contig_free_bits and marks group_bh dirty. It then takes write access on bm_bh: if that fails it rolls back (backup bitmap bits via ocfs2_calc_new_backup_super with set = 0, bg_free_bits_count and bg_bits restored, bg_contig_free_bits restored) and returns the error. Otherwise it adds num_bits to the chain record's c_total and c_free and to bitmap1.i_total, adds new_clusters to i_clusters, and for backups reduces c_free and increases i_used by the backup count; under ip_lock it updates ip_clusters and i_size by new_clusters << s_clustersize_bits, calls i_size_write, and marks bm_bh dirty. The counts added to the group and chain record are in bits (new_clusters * cl_bpc), not in clusters, and the chain record is the one named by group->bg_chain. Inode i_used is increased only by the backup superblock count.
note: slice cut head (function at 77-176, slice 1-259). reviewers: original right (the bit counts added are new_clusters * cl_bpc, 111-113, 144-146); round 2 right (c_free and i_used are updated, 145 and 150-151, and num_bits is a u16 so overflow is not guarded).

name: ocfs2_group_add
prose: Precondition: inode is any inode of the mounted ocfs2 filesystem, input describes a new, already formatted block group (group block number, chain, clusters, frees) to attach to the global bitmap (ocfs2/resize.c:458-598, int ocfs2_group_add(struct inode *inode, struct ocfs2_new_group_input *input)). Postcondition: returns 0 on success or a negative errno; -EROFS at line 474 if the filesystem is hard or soft read-only (before anything is taken), otherwise 'return ret' at 597 after the unwinding labels. Errors: -EINVAL if the global bitmap system inode cannot be obtained or if the bitmap's chain size is not the size implied by the block size ('disk is too old and small', 495-502); the error of ocfs2_inode_lock on the bitmap inode (the VFS inode lock taken first is released at out_mutex); the error of ocfs2_read_blocks_sync for the group descriptor; the error of ocfs2_verify_group_and_input; -EINVAL if ocfs2_start_trans fails (the group buffer is then removed from the cache); the error of ocfs2_journal_access_gd or ocfs2_journal_access_di (the group's bg_next_group is restored if the second one fails). On the main path it links the new group to the head of the chosen chain (group->bg_next_group = cr->c_blkno), increments cl_next_free_rec and clears the chain record if input->chain equals cl_next_free_rec, points the chain record at the new group, and adds to c_total, c_free, bitmap1.i_total (clusters * cl_bpc), i_used ((clusters - frees) * cl_bpc) and i_clusters, updates the cached cluster count and i_size, and calls ocfs2_update_super_and_backups. out_commit commits the transaction (only reached once the handle exists); at out_remove_cache, if ret < 0, the group buffer is removed from the inode cache (this also happens when starting the transaction failed, before any transaction was open, and for failures after the transaction started); the group buffer, bitmap buffer and cluster lock are released and the VFS lock and the system inode reference dropped before returning.
note: slice cut head (function at 458-598, slice 511-598). reviewer round 15 right: the ocfs2_start_trans failure at resize.c:522-527 jumps to out_remove_cache with ret = -EINVAL and no transaction open, so the cache removal at 580-582 is not only after a started transaction.

name: namevalue_size
prose: Precondition: name_len is a non-negative name length and value_len the value length in bytes; the sums must not overflow an int (ocfs2/xattr.c:214-220, static int namevalue_size(int name_len, uint64_t value_len)). Postcondition: has two return statements. If value_len > OCFS2_XATTR_INLINE_SIZE (80) it returns OCFS2_XATTR_SIZE(name_len) + OCFS2_XATTR_ROOT_SIZE, where OCFS2_XATTR_ROOT_SIZE is sizeof(struct ocfs2_xattr_def_value_root) (xattr.c:75), i.e. the name rounded up plus the size of the value root stored in place of an out-of-line value. Otherwise it returns OCFS2_XATTR_SIZE(name_len) + OCFS2_XATTR_SIZE(value_len). OCFS2_XATTR_SIZE(size) rounds its argument up to a multiple of 4 bytes (OCFS2_XATTR_ROUND is 3, ocfs2_fs.h:1054-1055), not 8. The function reads and writes no state.
note: slice does not include the function start (function at 214-220, slice 1-252 includes it). reviewers: round 2 right in part: the root size is sizeof(struct ocfs2_xattr_def_value_root), I did not verify its numeric value so it is given symbolically (the old 48/56 claims are not repeated); round 15 right: the rounding macro rounds to 4 bytes (ocfs2_fs.h:1054-1055); round 1 right that an overflow bound has to be stated for the sum. Contract left empty because OCFS2_XATTR_SIZE and the struct size are macros the verifier cannot see.

name: ocfs2_xa_check_space_helper
prose: Precondition: needed_space is the number of bytes wanted, free_start the offset where free space ends (bytes from the start of the xattr block), num_entries the current number of xattr entries (ocfs2/xattr.c:1432-1450, static int ocfs2_xa_check_space_helper(int needed_space, int free_start, int num_entries)). Postcondition: has three return points: 0 at line 1438 if needed_space is 0 (nothing is computed); -EIO at 1445 if the computed free space is negative; -ENOSPC at 1447 if the free space is smaller than needed_space; otherwise 0 at 1449. The free space is free_start - sizeof(struct ocfs2_xattr_header) - num_entries * sizeof(struct ocfs2_xattr_entry) - OCFS2_XATTR_HEADER_GAP; the subtraction uses unsigned size_t operands and the result is converted to the int free_space, so a result below zero (more header and entries than free_start) is detected through that conversion and gives -EIO (a corrupt block), while 0 <= free_space < needed_space gives -ENOSPC. It reads and writes no state.
note: slice cut head (function at 1432-1450, slice 1285-1540). Mechanical reviewers only (EIO/ENOSPC not in contract); contract left empty because of the struct sizes and the unsigned-to-int conversion.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE4(openat2, int, dfd, const char __user *, filename,
prose: Generated system call openat2(dfd, filename, how, usize) (open.c:1471-1496). Return values: -EINVAL if usize < OPEN_HOW_SIZE_VER0 (1481); -E2BIG if usize > PAGE_SIZE (1483); the result of copy_struct_from_user(&tmp, sizeof(tmp), how, usize) if non-zero (1487): -EFAULT if the user buffer cannot be read, -E2BIG if usize is larger than the struct and the extra bytes are non-zero (the reviewer's point, not -EINVAL); otherwise it records the how in the audit record, adds O_LARGEFILE when force_o_largefile() is true and O_PATH is not set, and returns do_sys_openat2(dfd, filename, &tmp). do_sys_openat2 (open.c:1420-1447) first calls build_open_flags (errors below), then getname (error pointer returned as its errno, e.g. -EFAULT, -ENAMETOOLONG, -ENOENT for an empty name), then get_unused_fd_flags (negative result such as -EMFILE returned), then do_filp_open: on failure the reserved fd is released (put_unused_fd) and the error is returned, else the file is installed with fd_install and the new fd number returned; the name is putname'd on every path after getname. build_open_flags (open.c:1238-1361) returns -EINVAL for invalid flag bits, invalid resolve bits, BENEATH together with IN_ROOT, a mode given without O_CREAT/O_TMPFILE or with bits outside S_IALLUGO, O_DIRECTORY with O_CREAT, __O_TMPFILE without O_DIRECTORY or without write access, O_PATH with flags other than the allowed set, and -EAGAIN for RESOLVE_CACHED combined with O_TRUNC, O_CREAT or __O_TMPFILE.
note: macro-generated; the C function is generated by the SYSCALL_DEFINE/COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE macro at the line cited, and the packet name (sys_/__x64_ prefix) is not text in the file; name set to the macro head. Reviewer round 15 right: copy_struct_from_user failures are -EFAULT or -E2BIG (open.c:1485-1487), and build_open_flags errors are returned through do_sys_openat2.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE3(open, const char __user *, filename, int, flags, umode_t, mode)
prose: Generated compat system call open(filename, flags, mode) (open.c:1503-1506): returns do_sys_open(AT_FDCWD, filename, flags, mode) without adding O_LARGEFILE. do_sys_open (open.c:1449-1453) builds a struct open_how with build_open_how (flags masked with VALID_OPEN_FLAGS, mode with S_IALLUGO, O_PATH reduces the flags to the O_PATH-compatible set, and the mode is cleared when no creation flag is present) and returns do_sys_openat2(dfd, filename, &how). do_sys_openat2 (open.c:1420-1447) first calls build_open_flags (errors below), then getname (error pointer returned as its errno, e.g. -EFAULT, -ENAMETOOLONG, -ENOENT for an empty name), then get_unused_fd_flags (negative result such as -EMFILE returned), then do_filp_open: on failure the reserved fd is released (put_unused_fd) and the error is returned, else the file is installed with fd_install and the new fd number returned; the name is putname'd on every path after getname. build_open_flags (open.c:1238-1361) returns -EINVAL for invalid flag bits, invalid resolve bits, BENEATH together with IN_ROOT, a mode given without O_CREAT/O_TMPFILE or with bits outside S_IALLUGO, O_DIRECTORY with O_CREAT, __O_TMPFILE without O_DIRECTORY or without write access, O_PATH with flags other than the allowed set, and -EAGAIN for RESOLVE_CACHED combined with O_TRUNC, O_CREAT or __O_TMPFILE.
note: macro-generated; the C function is generated by the SYSCALL_DEFINE/COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE macro at the line cited, and the packet name (sys_/__x64_ prefix) is not text in the file; name set to the macro head. Reviewer right: build_open_flags validation errors (e.g. -EINVAL) can be returned.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE4(openat, int, dfd, const char __user *, filename, int, flags, umode_t, mode)
prose: Generated compat system call openat(dfd, filename, flags, mode) (open.c:1512-1515): returns do_sys_open(dfd, filename, flags, mode), without adding O_LARGEFILE; dfd may be AT_FDCWD or an open directory fd (an invalid dfd gives an error from do_filp_open, such as -EBADF). do_sys_open (open.c:1449-1453) calls build_open_how on flags and mode and then do_sys_openat2. do_sys_openat2 (open.c:1420-1447) first calls build_open_flags (errors below), then getname (error pointer returned as its errno, e.g. -EFAULT, -ENAMETOOLONG, -ENOENT for an empty name), then get_unused_fd_flags (negative result such as -EMFILE returned), then do_filp_open: on failure the reserved fd is released (put_unused_fd) and the error is returned, else the file is installed with fd_install and the new fd number returned; the name is putname'd on every path after getname. build_open_flags (open.c:1238-1361) returns -EINVAL for invalid flag bits, invalid resolve bits, BENEATH together with IN_ROOT, a mode given without O_CREAT/O_TMPFILE or with bits outside S_IALLUGO, O_DIRECTORY with O_CREAT, __O_TMPFILE without O_DIRECTORY or without write access, O_PATH with flags other than the allowed set, and -EAGAIN for RESOLVE_CACHED combined with O_TRUNC, O_CREAT or __O_TMPFILE.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE2(creat, const char __user *, pathname, umode_t, mode)
prose: Generated system call creat(pathname, mode) (open.c:1524-1531, compiled unless __alpha__): sets flags = O_CREAT | O_WRONLY | O_TRUNC, adds O_LARGEFILE when force_o_largefile() is true, and returns do_sys_open(AT_FDCWD, pathname, flags, mode). The result is the new file descriptor (>= 0) or a negative errno from the open path (name copy errors, -EMFILE, errors from build_open_flags and do_filp_open such as -EACCES, -ENOENT, -EISDIR, -EROFS, -ENOSPC, -EPERM). Because O_EXCL is not set, -EEXIST is not produced by this call itself (the reviewer's objection is right, open.c:1526). The mode is masked with S_IALLUGO by build_open_how.
note: macro-generated; the C function is generated by the SYSCALL_DEFINE/COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE macro at the line cited, and the packet name (sys_/__x64_ prefix) is not text in the file; name set to the macro head. Reviewer round 1 right: no O_EXCL, so creat cannot return -EEXIST for an existing file.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE1(close, unsigned int, fd)
prose: Generated system call close(fd) (open.c:1574-1602). It removes fd from the current process's descriptor table with file_close_fd(fd) (file.c:850-860, under files->file_lock); if there is no file it returns -EBADF (1581) and nothing else changes. Otherwise the table entry is already cleared; it calls filp_flush(file, current->files) (the file's ->flush op and, for non-O_PATH files, dnotify and POSIX-lock removal; the flush result is kept in retval) and then fput_close_sync(file) to drop the table's reference. If retval is 0 it returns 0 (1592); otherwise the flush error is returned, except that -ERESTARTSYS, -ERESTARTNOINTR, -ERESTARTNOHAND and -ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK are converted to -EINTR (a restart is impossible because the descriptor is already released). So the descriptor is released on every path except the -EBADF one, where there was no file to release, and even when a flush error is returned.
note: macro-generated; the C function is generated by the SYSCALL_DEFINE/COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE macro at the line cited, and the packet name (sys_/__x64_ prefix) is not text in the file; name set to the macro head. Reviewer round 1 right: the prose should not say the entry is released on -EBADF (there was nothing to release); -EBADF is returned when file_close_fd finds no file.

name: orangefs_bufmap_copy_to_iovec
prose: Precondition: the global buffer map __orangefs_bufmap is initialised, buffer_index is a valid index into its desc_array, whose page_array holds enough pages for size bytes, and iter is a destination iov_iter (orangefs/orangefs-bufmap.c:498-522, int orangefs_bufmap_copy_to_iovec(struct iov_iter *iter, int buffer_index, size_t size); the packet name orangefs_bufmap_copy_to_iter is not in the file). Postcondition: copies size bytes from the shared-memory pages of the selected descriptor to iter, one page (at most PAGE_SIZE bytes) at a time with copy_page_to_iter, and returns 0 when all size bytes were copied (line 521). If a copy_page_to_iter call copies nothing (n == 0) it returns -EFAULT at 518 immediately; a short non-zero copy is not an error here: size is reduced by the amount copied and the loop continues with the next page (so after a short copy, the next page's data continues to be copied from offset 0 of the next page, and the pages are indexed by loop count i, not by bytes consumed). The iterator is advanced by what was copied; the buffer map itself is not modified.
note: slice cut head (function at 498-522; slice 505-522 is its body). The packet name orangefs_bufmap_copy_to_iter does not exist; the real name is orangefs_bufmap_copy_to_iovec. The short-copy behaviour (517-519, 516-519) is as coded: only n == 0 is treated as an error.

name: ovl_verify_area
prose: Precondition: none; pos, pos2, len and totlen are any loff_t (signed 64-bit) values (overlayfs/copy_up.c:232-243, static int ovl_verify_area(loff_t pos, loff_t pos2, loff_t len, loff_t totlen)). Postcondition: returns -EIO (line 237) if pos != pos2; -EIO (239) if pos, len or totlen is negative; -EIO (241) if pos + len would overflow a loff_t (check_add_overflow); otherwise 0 (242). So the result is 0 exactly when pos == pos2, all of pos, len and totlen are non-negative and pos + len does not exceed the largest loff_t, and -EIO otherwise. totlen is only checked for being non-negative. The function reads and writes no state.
contract: /*@ requires \true; ensures ((pos == pos2 && pos >= 0 && len >= 0 && totlen >= 0 && pos <= 9223372036854775807LL - len) ==> \result == 0) && (!(pos == pos2 && pos >= 0 && len >= 0 && totlen >= 0 && pos <= 9223372036854775807LL - len) ==> \result == -5); */
note: slice cut head (function at 232-243, slice 1-253). Mechanical reviewers only. The contract uses EIO = 5 (Linux errno value) and the signed 64-bit maximum; it is for a pure function of four integers, per rule 4. If the verifier objects to the literal -5, the contract can be dropped without loss to the prose.

name: ovl_remove_and_whiteout
prose: Precondition: dentry is an overlayfs dentry whose parent has an upper directory, list is the (possibly empty) list of merged directory entries of dentry (non-empty for a merged directory being removed), and the caller holds the parent's directory lock as required by ovl_cleanup_and_whiteout (overlayfs/dir.c:789-833, static int). Postcondition: returns 0 or a negative errno; the single return is 'return err' at 832. Errors: -EROFS (after a WARN_ON) at 800 if there is no work directory; if list is non-empty it calls ovl_clear_empty(dentry, list) to replace the directory by an empty opaque one, and an error pointer from it is returned as err without any dput (nothing was obtained); the error of ovl_lookup_upper_unlocked for the child name (going to out_dput, which dputs opaquedir if one was created); -ESTALE if the upper dentry found does not match (it must equal the opaque directory when one exists, or match the dentry's own upper dentry via ovl_matches_upper when there is no opaque directory but the dentry has an upper), in which case it does not call d_drop; otherwise err = ovl_cleanup_and_whiteout(ofs, upperdir, upper) (creates a whiteout in place of the upper entry via the work directory); on success ovl_dir_modified(dentry->d_parent, true) is called. After the whiteout step, d_drop(dentry) is executed whether or not ovl_cleanup_and_whiteout succeeded (line 826). Then the upper dentry reference and the opaque directory reference (if any) are dropped with dput, and err is returned.
note: slice cut head (function at 789-833, slice 784-1047). reviewers: round 1 right (the ovl_clear_empty error goes to out and skips dput(opaquedir), 805-806, since nothing was held); round 2 right (d_drop at 826 runs even if ovl_cleanup_and_whiteout failed, because only the -ESTALE and lookup-error paths jump past it).

name: ovl_get_inode
prose: Precondition: sb is an overlayfs superblock and oip describes the inode to get: oip->upperdentry (may be NULL), oip->oe (the lower layers; at least one of upper or lower must exist), oip->newinode (a preallocated inode or NULL), redirect strings, index and lowerdata flags (overlayfs/inode.c:1210-1315, struct inode *ovl_get_inode(struct super_block *sb, struct ovl_inode_params *oip); the packet item was the unnamed tail of it). Postcondition: returns the inode (a pointer, possibly one already in the inode cache) or ERR_PTR(err); the single return is 'return inode' at line 1309, reached directly or via out_err which logs 'failed to get inode (%i)' (ratelimited) and sets ERR_PTR(err). err starts as -EEXIST when oip->newinode is given, otherwise -ENOMEM. It chooses the real inode (upper, else lower) and whether to hash by the lower inode (ovl_hash_bylower). prose: Generated compat system call getdents(fd, dirent, count) (readdir.c:567-595, under CONFIG_COMPAT): reads directory entries of fd into the user buffer dirent of count bytes in compat_linux_dirent format and returns the number of bytes filled or a negative errno. name: do_signalfd4
prose: Precondition: mask points to a writable sigset_t that this function modifies in place (it clears the SIGKILL and SIGSTOP bits and complements the set; that normalisation is done by the function, not required of the caller), ufd is -1 to create a new signalfd or the descriptor of an existing signalfd, flags may contain any bits (signalfd.c:~250-304, static int do_signalfd4(int ufd, sigset_t *mask, int flags); slice cut head). Postcondition: returns the signalfd descriptor (ufd, or a new descriptor number) or a negative errno. -EINVAL at line 260 if flags has bits other than SFD_CLOEXEC and SFD_NONBLOCK, returned before the mask is touched; then the mask is modified (sigdelsetmask of KILL and STOP, then signotset). If ufd == -1: kmalloc of the context (-ENOMEM at 270), ctx->sigmask = *mask, get_unused_fd_flags(flags & O_CLOEXEC) (its negative result returned after freeing the context, 277), anon_inode_getfile_fmode (an error pointer returns PTR_ERR after releasing the fd and context, 286); otherwise fd_install and the new descriptor is returned at 303. If ufd is an existing descriptor: -EBADF at 292 if it is not open, -EINVAL at 295 if its file is not a signalfd, else the stored signal mask is replaced under current->sighand->siglock and the signalfd wait queue woken; ufd is returned at 303.
note: slice cut head (the function starts a few lines before the slice, at about signalfd.c:250). reviewers: original right (the mask normalisation at 262-263 is done by the function); round 2 right (an unopened fd gives -EBADF at 292, not -EINVAL); round 15 right (the flags check at 259-260 precedes the mask modification).

The mask is a local copy, so the user buffer is not modified.
